chunks: Saad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa and Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Ali ibn Riab, from Ubaydullah ibn Ali al-Halabi, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) remained in Mecca for thirteen years after the revelation came to him from Allah, the Exalted. Among these, three years were spent in secret, fearful, not appearing openly, until Allah commanded him to proclaim openly what he was ordered to do. At that time, he publicized the call.

key_terms.يُصَدِّعَ: To proclaim openly / to make public

ai.seo_question: How long did the Prophet Muhammad stay in Mecca after receiving revelation, and when did he begin preaching openly?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* details the thirteen-year Meccan period of the Prophet’s mission, emphasizing a crucial three-year phase of *satr* (concealment* where he preached quietly due to fear before receiving the divine command to 'proclaim openly' (Surah Al-Hijr 15:94). This historical progression from secrecy to public declaration serves as a foundational model for the Imam of the Age, illustrating how the Master of the Affair may remain in concealment before his eventual reappearance.
